name: Clare Market
text: Clare Market is a historic area in central London located within the parish of St Clement Danes to the west of Lincoln's Inn Fields, between the Strand and Drury Lane, with Vere Street adjoining its western side. It was named after the food market which had been established in Clement's Inn Fields, by John Holles, 2nd Earl of Clare. Much of the area and its landmarks were immortalised by Charles Dickens in The Old Curiosity Shop, The Pickwick Papers, Barnaby Rudge and Sketches by Boz.

depictions.name: Clare Market
depictions.text: Clare Market was an area in London, United Kingdom during the Victorian era. The area around Clare Market was spared by the Great Fire of London in 1666, and several Elizabethan buildings could still be found here. The Blighters, operating under Victor Lynch, took the area near the food market for themselves, and used it to establish one of their two strongholds in the Strand.
